beats.t: By morning, the library had fallen quiet as though it had never been wet. Dried books lay open in rows on every reading desk beneath the domed ceiling.
Book one hundred and twelve. Pig, know what I'm doing with fire right now? Drying books. Me, a chef.
Good work. Five stars. Ironing service added.
Pay me in food, not stars. Can't eat stars.
With each ember Moka rolled, the damp pages unfurled softly. Something like the scent of warm bread rose from them.
Lovely smell. It must be a book about someone's birthday morning.
You can tell that from how a book smells?
No. Just saying things. Sounds convincing, though.
See? A con artist starts scamming first thing in the morning.
And Mr. Otter starts remembering me first thing. Thank you.
Don't put it like that. I can't even get mad.
The baby dragon wriggled off Yeoni's wrist. Its belly was round and swollen, and tiny droplets flew out whenever it yawned.
Look at this one. Still digesting yesterday's flood.
If a dragon gets an upset stomach from drinking water, what kind of weather is that? Monsoon?
A storehouse that isn't full is good news. It means it can drink the next flood, too.
Hear that? You're our team's official water purifier.
Apparently pleased, the baby dragon curled its tail once around Yeoni's hoof and fell asleep again.
At the end of the desk, Yeoni opened their hoof. The eight-slot chart appeared. Seven spaces were filled, one of them frozen black.
[ Year 壬午 · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ]  7/8
(Only one left. But where do I find this blank?)
Yundal, this last slot. The first character of the Hour Pillar. What kind of place is it?
Since your Day Master is Eul Wood, the character that can go there is fixed. Gyeong Metal—庚. The place of Influence.
Influence. The one after Expression, Wealth, and Resources?
Yes. The energy that governs and protects you. Rules, responsibility, things like name tags.
But it's strange. We found all the other characters on islands. There wasn't an Island of Influence.
No chart is without Influence. If you can't see it, it's hiding.
Yeoni remembered the first day. Fog over the river, and lights rising beyond it.
(Yeongnyangi said it then. The characters of your Four Pillars are scattered across four islands.)
Blue light, flickering firelight, golden light, and a light like old bookshelves. There had definitely been four.
There were four islands. Companions, Expression, Wealth, Resources. But there are five groups among the Ten Stars.
You've been studying, my lady. Care for a part-time job at my compatibility booth?
That's not what we're talking about.
Where'd the fifth light go, then? Someone pocket it?
Gyeong Metal is a blade, iron. Hard, cold, straight. The most difficult counterpart for Eul Wood.
A difficult counterpart has to sit in my slot?
When a difficult counterpart becomes your partner, the bond is the strongest. Eul and Gyeong are drawn to each other.
(Cold, straight iron. Why does someone keep coming to mind?)
Then the reading room door opened. Yeongnyangi came in. His fur was half dry, and he hesitated very slightly with each step on his left paw.
Yeongnyangi, perfect timing. At the start, you said there were four islands. Where's the fifth?
It isn't here now.
Isn't here? But there are five groups?
Customer Support is closed.
Every time you say that, I'm deducting a star.
Yeongnyangi sat at the far end of the desk. Normally, he would have sat beside Yeoni. Yeoni glanced at that empty place.
(He's been like this since yesterday. Every time I move closer, he steps back.)
Mr. Cat, may I ask when your birthday is?
Why?
Habit. I ask everyone I meet. Especially those who stay beside our lady.
I don't know.
You don't know. Interesting in itself.
Con artist, you're testing the cat, aren't you? Even I can see that.
Yeoni rose and slowly walked between the desks, the chart floating over their hoof.
One experiment. Everyone stay still.
What now? Pig experiments usually end with me getting hurt.
Yeoni went to Moka. The blank stayed quiet. Then to Yundal. It trembled ever so slightly, then stilled again.
My hour is empty, too. Just two empty spaces saying hello.
Finally, Yeoni walked toward Yeongnyangi. One step, two. The blank grew brighter.
Directly before Yeongnyangi, it blazed white. Like sunlight striking cold iron.
It did this yesterday. It's doing it today. Still my imagination?
Light naturally goes toward brightness. It's because my fur is white.
I've never heard such a ridiculous excuse.
Yeoni. Step back.
Why? What's wrong with me getting close?
Instead of answering, Yeongnyangi pushed back his chair and stood. The blank's glow sharply dimmed, matching the distance he had put between them.
It's nothing. Just tired today.
Yeongnyangi left the reading room. The closing door sounded unusually loud.
Hey, what's with that cat lately? He was always obnoxious, but now his obnoxiousness looks sad.
I don't know. Whenever I ask, he says later.
Yundal watched the door for a long time. His gloved fingers tapped the desk twice.
My lady. In a woman's chart, Influence has another meaning.
What is it?
Ah, I'll tell you next time. If I say it now, I think you might bang your head on the desk.
Now I'm even more curious!
Me too. Tell us. Or I'll burn your glove.
Then it's even more of a secret.
All afternoon, Yeoni wandered the library searching for the fifth light. Moka grumbled along behind.
It's a library. If you don't know something, look it up. Let's try the catalog desk.
That chatty card cabinet from the first day? It's the one that told me to be quiet.
The catalog desk's drawers rattled open as soon as they saw the pair. One card flew out and stopped before Yeoni's nose.
[ Please state your search terms · Borrowing allowance: 0/1 ]
Flower Pig. Influence. Fifth light.
The writing on the card spread like ink, then gathered again. This time, the result was a single line.
[ No results · Location: Outside the library · Contact: Customer Support ]
Customer Support?
What's Customer Support? They have that here?
They do. From the very first day. Customer Support that accepts neither complaints nor worries.
Yeoni turned the card over. Its back was blank. No—one very faint pawprint marked it.
That's a cat paw. Look at the size. I know because he puts that paw on my skewers all the time.
(Four islands. The fifth light isn't an island. It's outside the library. Contact: Customer Support.)
Moka. Is there anything about Yeongnyangi you haven't told me?
Huh? No. Why ask me? I'm an otter. Otters don't know about secrets.
Your tail is wagging incredibly fast.
I'm drying my fur! It got wet drying the books!
Moka hurried off toward another shelf. Yeoni watched him go for a long time.
(Moka knows, too. Yundal looked like he knew. I'm the only one who doesn't.)
That night, everyone slept in a small room deep inside the library. Moka snored with his head on a book pillow.
(Can't sleep. I keep thinking about that blank.)
Tossing and turning, Yeoni looked toward the corner. The spot where Yeongnyangi always curled up to sleep was empty.
Yeongnyangi?
No answer. Yeoni pushed back the blanket and sat up. Between Moka's snores, they could hear their own heartbeat.
A few strands of white fur and a note lay in the empty spot. A pawprint served as a signature.
[ Back soon. Worries not accepted. · Customer Support ]
What kind of note is this? Why won't you accept worries?!
(Since when does our Customer Support close without a word like this?)
Yeoni stood, holding the note. The baby dragon on their wrist opened sleepy eyes, then turned toward the window.
Rain sounded outside. The sky was clear, but the smell of rain was there.
I know that smell.
(The smell from the drowned shelves, from above the chains. A wet cloak.)
Yeoni folded the note and clutched it tightly. Then they opened the window without a sound.
Hanging from the frame, Yeoni looked up. Two shadows stood at the top of the rounded roof.
One was a white cat in a hat. Even beneath the half-eaten sun, the hat's crescent shone gold.
The other was a black tiger. Rainwater dripped without cease from the hem of its soaked cloak.
Why are they together? Are they fighting?
The baby dragon bit down hard on Yeoni's hoof. Whether it meant don't go or hurry, Yeoni couldn't tell.
Okay. I'll be quiet. Hold your breath, too.
They were not fighting. They stood a little apart, facing the same direction. Like two who had known each other a long time.
The wind blew. Yeongnyangi's eyes flashed gold. A blade-like gleam cut across the roof and vanished.
(Yeongnyangi. Whose side are you on right now?)
Just as Yeoni was about to climb over the window frame, both shadows on the roof turned toward them at once.
